questions.q:
A total of $48 \mathrm{~J}$ heat is given to one mole of helium kept in a cylinder. The temperature of helium increases by $2^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$. The work done by the gas is:
Given, $\mathrm{R}=8.3 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$1^{\text {st }}$ law of thermodynamics
$\begin{aligned}
& \Delta \mathrm{Q}=\Delta \mathrm{U}+\mathrm{W} \\
& \Rightarrow+48=\mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{v}} \Delta \mathrm{T}+\mathrm{W} \\
& \Rightarrow 48=(1)\left(\frac{3 \mathrm{R}}{2}\right)(2)+\mathrm{W} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{W}=48-3 \times \mathrm{R} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{W}=48-3 \times(8.3) \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{W}=23.1 \text { Joule }
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Heat energy of $735J$ is given to a diatomic gas allowing the gas to expand at constant pressure. Each gas molecule rotates around an internal axis but do not oscillate. The increase in the internal energy of the gas will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For isobaric process and diatomic gas we can write,& $\Delta Q = n{C}_{P}\Delta T = 735J$

$⇒ n\dfrac{7R}{2}\Delta T = 735J ⇒ nR\Delta T = 210$

Now internal energy will be,

$\Delta U = n{C}_{V}\Delta T = n\dfrac{5R}{2}\Delta T = \dfrac{5}{2} \times 210$

$= 525J$

questions.q: In thermodynamics, heat and work are :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Heat and work are treated as path functions in thermodynamics.

$\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$

Since work done by gas depends on type of process i.e. path and $\Delta U$~depends just on initial and final states, so $\Delta Q$ i.e. heat, also has to depend on process is path.

questions.q:
Statement - I : When $\mu$ amount of an ideal gas undergoes adiabatic change from state \left({P}_{1}, {V}_{1}, {T}_{1}\right)$ to state \left({P}_{2}, {V}_{2}, {T}_{2}\right)$, then work done is $W = \dfrac{\muR\left({T}_{2} - {T}_{1}\right)}{1 - \gamma}$, where $\gamma = \dfrac{CP}{CV}$ and~$R =$ universal gas constant.

Statement - II : In the above case, when work is done on the gas, the temperature of the gas would rise.
options: Both statement-I and statement-II are true.
Both statement-I and statement-II are false.
Statement-I is true but statement-II is false.
Statement-I is false but statement-II is true.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The work done in an adiabatic process is given by,

${W}_{adiabatic} = \dfrac{nR\left({T}_{f} - {T}_{i}\right)}{1 - \gamma} \to$ statement~I is true.

For adiabatic process~$∆ Q = 0$. From the first law of thermodynamics,

$∆ Q = W + \Delta U$

$0 = W + \Delta U$

$\Delta U = - W$

If work is done on the gas, i.e. work is negative

$∴ \Delta U$ is positive.

$∴$& The temperature will increase. Hence, statement II is also true.

questions.q: During the melting of a slab of ice at 273 K at atmospheric pressure :
options: Internal energy of ice-water system remains unchanged.
Positive work is done by the ice-water system on the atmosphere.
Internal energy of the ice-water system decreases.
Positive work is done on the ice-water system by the atmosphere.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Volume decreases during melting of ice so positive work is done on ice water system by atmosphere
Heat absorbed by ice water so $\Delta \mathrm{Q}$ is positive, work done by ice water system is negative
Hence by first law of thermodynamics
$\Delta \mathrm{U}=\Delta \mathrm{Q}+\Delta \mathrm{W}=\text { Positive }$
So internal energy increases

questions.q:
A gas can be taken from $A$ to $B$ via two different processes $ACB$ and $ADB$.



When path $ACB$ is used $60J$ of heat flows into the system and $30J$ of work is done by the system. If the path $ADB$ is~used then work done by the system is $10J$, the heat flows into the system in the path $ADB$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For path $ACB$,

$\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$

$60 = \Delta U + 30$

$⇒ \Delta U = 30J$

For path $ADB$

$\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$

As initial and find points are the same, change in internal energy is same in both the cases

$\Delta Q = 30 + 10$

$= 40J$

The change in the internal energy of the gas along the path $ca$ is $- 180J .$ The gas absorbs $250J$ of heat along the path $ab$ and $60J$ along the path $bc$ . The work done by the gas along the path $abc$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In a cyclic process, $\Delta U = 0$
From 1st law of thermodynamics
$Q = \Delta U + W$
$Q = W$
${Q}_{ab} + {Q}_{bc} + {Q}_{ca} = {W}_{abc} + {W}_{ca}$
${W}_{abc} = {Q}_{ab} + {Q}_{bc} + {Q}_{ca} - {W}_{ca}$
${W}_{abc} = {Q}_{ab} + {Q}_{bc} + {U}_{ca}$
${W}_{abc} = 250 + 60 - 180 = 130J$

questions.q:
Match List I with List II :

List I List II
A Isothermal Process I Work done by the gas decreases internal energy
B Adiabatic Process II No change in internal energy
C Isochoric Process III The heat absorbed goes partly to increase internal energy and partly to do work
D Isobaric Process IV No work is done on or by the gas

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) Change in internal energy is expressed as$∆ U = n{C}_{v} ∆ T$, here,~$∆ T$~is change in temperature.

Since, in an isothermal process temperature remains~constant, thus,~$∆ U = 0$

$A \to II$

(B) In an adiabatic process, heat transfer,~$Q = 0$.

So, from first law of thermodynamics,~

$Q = ∆ U + W$

$∆ U = - W$

Since, work done by gas is positive, thus,~$∆ U$ is negative

$B \to I$

(C) In an isochoric process, volume remains constant, so work done by or on the gas~$W = P ∆ V = 0$

$C \to IV$

(D) In an isobaric process, pressure remains constant, so work done$W = P ∆ V \ne 0$~and~change in internal energy~$∆ U = n{C}_{v} ∆ T \ne 0$

Thus, heat absorbed goes partly to increase internal energy and partly do work.

$D \to III$

questions.q:
A thermally insulated vessel contains an ideal gas of molecular mass $M$~and ratio of specific heats $1 . 4$. Vessel is moving with speed $v$ and is suddenly brought to rest. Assuming no heat is lost to the surrounding and vessel temperature of the gas increases by :
($R =$& universal gas constant)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
KE of the vessel $= \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

When the vessel is suddenly stopped, the ordered motion of the gas molecules is converted into disordered motion of the molecules increasing thereby the internal energy of the gas. Thus,

$∆ U = n{C}_{v} ∆ T = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(nM\right)v^{2}$

Where $n$ is number of moles of the gas in the vessel and $M$ is molecular weight of the gas.

$∴ ∆ T = \dfrac{Mv^{2}}{2{C}_{v}}$

As ${C}_{v} = \dfrac{R}{\gamma - 1}$

$∴ ∆ T = \dfrac{Mv^{2} ( \gamma - 1 )}{2R} = \dfrac{Mv^{2} ( 1 . 4 - 1 )}{2R} = \dfrac{Mv^{2}}{5R}$

questions.q:
Heat is given to an ideal gas in an isothermal process.

A. Internal energy of the gas will decrease.

B. Internal energy of the gas will increase.

C. Internal energy of the gas will not change.

D. The gas will do positive work.

E. The gas will do negative work.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the first law of thermodynamics, heat supplied to the system& $Q$, change in internal energy of the system~$∆ U$~and work done by the system~$W$~are related as:

$Q = ∆ U + W$

Since the process is isothermal, the temperature of the system is constant and therefore~$∆ U = 0$~(i.e., internal energy is constant).~

$⇒ Q = W$

As heat is supplied to the system,~$Q$~is positive and therefore~$W$& is positivei.e., gas will do positive work.

Hence, correct options are C and D.

questions.q: An electric appliance supplies $6000J\min^{- 1}$, heat to the system. If the system delivers a power of $90W$. How long it would take to increase the internal energy by~$2 . 5 \times {10}^{3}J$?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Recall the formula of the first law of thermodynamics in terms of change in internal energy and work done by the system,& $\Delta U = Q - W$, given,~$\Delta U = 2500J$,~$Q = \dfrac{6000}{60} \times t = \left(100t\right)J$~and~$W = P \times t = 90t$,~
$⇒ 2500J = 100tJ - 90tJ ⇒ t = 2 . 5 \times {10}^{2}s$.

questions.q: In an Isothermal change, the change in pressure and volume of a gas can be represented for three different temperature;& ${T}_{3} > {T}_{2} > {T}_{1}$& as:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In case of isothermal process, pressure vs volume graph is a rectangular hyperbola.

The graph of the isothermal process shifts away from the origin as the temperature of the process is increased. Thus, the curve away from the& origin ${T}_{3}$ have the highest temperature whereas the curve closer to the origin~${T}_{1}$ have the lowest temperature.

Here, the dotted line shows~the isobaric line that implies~${T}_{3} > {T}_{2} > {T}_{1}$~as $T = \dfrac{PV}{nR}$.

questions.q: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of $4moles$ of a rigid diatomic gas from $0 ° C$ to~$50 ° C$ when no work is done is$( R$ is the universal gas constant)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$
Here $\Delta W = 0$
$\Delta Q = \Delta U = n{C}_{V}\Delta T$
$\Delta Q = 4 \times \dfrac{5R}{2} ( 50 ) = 500R$
Hence option $( 4 ) .$

questions.q: The temperature of 1 mole of an ideal monoatomic gas is increased by $50^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ at constant pressure. The total heat added and change in internal energy are $E_1$ and $E_2$, respectively. If $\frac{E_1}{E_2}=\frac{x}{9}$ then the value of $x$ is _____
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that process is isobaric $\Delta \mathrm{T}=50^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$
Q in isobaric process $=\mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{p}} \Delta $\mathrm{T}=\mathrm{E}$_1\Delta \mathrm{U}$ in isobaric process $=\mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{v}} \Delta $\mathrm{T}=\mathrm{E}$_2\therefore \frac{\mathrm{E}_1}{\mathrm{E}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{P}}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}}=\gamma$ Given, gas is monoatomic
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \gamma & =1+\frac{2}{\mathrm{f}} \\
& =1+\frac{2}{3} \\
& =\frac{5}{3}
\end{aligned}$ Now, as per question.
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{5}{3}=\frac{x}{9} \\
& x=15
\end{aligned}$

[$R$& universal gas constant]

questions.q: A diatomic gas  \left(\gamma = 1 . 4\right)$ does $400J$ of work when it is expanded isobarically. The heat given to the gas in the process is _____~$J$.$

questions.solution:
For& isobaric process:& $W = nR\Delta T⇒ 400 = nR\Delta T$

Also:~$Q = n{C}_{p}\Delta T$~

~$⇒ Q = n\left(\dfrac{7R}{2}\right)\Delta T$~ (${C}_{p} = \dfrac{7R}{2}$, for diatomic gas)

$Q = \dfrac{7}{2} \times 400 = 1400J$
